answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making trust grow from verified work, like a grove that takes seasons to mature. New identities start with tasks whose outputs are checked by randomly assigned peers; only consistent correct work raises reputation, which decays without continued contribution. One cedar of proven history is worth more than an ocean of empty new accounts. An attacker flooding the network must pay the full cost of genuine work for every fake identity, and peer audits reject copied or low-effort output, so Sybil identities stay too weak and too expensive to matter.
